summary: Approximately 3,287,263 km² and about 1.33 billion people (2020), from Wikidata's Q668 (P2046, P1082). The English Wikipedia article "India", at revision 1375550105, opens: "India, officially the Republic of India, is a country in South Asia. It is the world's seventh-largest country by area and the largest by population. Bounded by the Indian Ocean on the south, the Arabian Sea on the southwest, and the Bay of Bengal on the southeast, it shares land borders with Pakistan to the west; China, Nepal, and Bhutan to the north; and Bangladesh and Myanmar to the east." That is the article's account and not yet this atlas's; nobody has read this record, and review.html is where somebody does. The Republic of India, independent from 1947, claimed the Portuguese territories on its coast — Goa, Daman, Diu, and the enclaves of Dadra and Nagar Haveli — from the beginning, and Portugal refused to negotiate on the ground that they were not colonies but part of Portugal. Diplomatic relations were broken in 1955, the enclaves were taken by volunteers the same year, and after years of blockade Indian forces occupied Goa, Daman and Diu in December 1961. Portugal recognised the loss only in 1974. It is in the atlas as the actor that ended Portuguese rule in Asia's mainland, and whose action hardened Lisbon's determination to hold Africa.
